title: Sophronius, Against Eunomius
english: The work of Sophronius likewise, on behalf of Basil against Eunomius, has been read by me. He is clearer than Theodore and much more concise, and does not go through every work of Eunomius; instead he exercises himself on those passages, and overthrows by refutation those which seem to hold his heresy together and to be its chief points. He employs an aphoristic manner, and in general his discourse is detached and disconnected — though not from want of judgment; rather, it is rounded off with logical arguments as well.
translator_notes: Greek locked from Bekker 1824; Freese 1920 used as PD English reference only.
Codex 5 of 279; Sophronius (fl. c. 400), probably friend of Jerome and translator of his works. 'Aphoristic' = asyndetos (without conjunctions).
Only essential points of Eunomius's heresy refuted; briefer than Theodore.
